plans.note: Cap sits in sec-21.1 (one month of Fees paid, 'without exception') which conflicts with the Excluded Claims regime in sec-21.3; assess cap quantum and whether carve-outs survive the 'without exception' language. 21.2/21.4 support the consequential-damages and severability analysis.

Only sec-20 appears, containing a broad Customer-side indemnity (20.1) for 'every claim'; no Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity is visible even though sec-9.3 cross-references a Section 20.5 remedy. Check whether a Vendor indemnity exists anywhere before deciding between deviation and missing.
sec-12.4 imposes a 24-month, worldwide non-compete on us — squarely a walk-away deviation; sec-12.3 says we made no non-compete commitment, so note the internal conflict.

sec-2.2 (first of two 2.2s) makes Vendor sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics; sec-12.3 disclaims any exclusivity commitment. Address the exclusivity grant and flag the numbering/conflict with sec-2.2-2.
No MFN obligation running against us appears; sec-12.3 expressly confirms no most-favoured-customer commitment. Likely nothing to redline.
No non-solicit binding us is apparent; sec-12.3 preserves hiring anyone responding to general recruitment and disclaims a no-hire commitment.

sec-9.4 gives us convenience termination on 30 days with refund of prepaid Fees and denies Vendor a matching right — favourable. Cross-check against the take-or-pay in sec-2.1, which purports to bar reduction or termination (handle that under MINCOMMIT).
sec-8.2 gives a 30-day opt-out plus a reminder mechanic; sec-8.3 caps uplift at lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice. Likely compliant; note any minor gaps rather than redlining.
New York law (sec-28.1) and exclusive New York County courts (sec-28.2), with a pre-suit executive escalation in sec-28.3 that preserves urgent relief — within accepted parameters.
sec-24.1 permits our affiliate/successor assignment without consent; sec-24.2 restricts Vendor; sec-24.4 blocks Vendor remedies on our change of control. sec-13.3 ties licence transfer to Section 24.

Customer ownership of Data and Deliverables in sec-14.1–14.2 with assignment from Vendor; check the Deliverable/Vendor Technology definitions (sec-1.4, sec-1.8) and the telemetry carve-out in sec-1.3 for scope leakage, plus sec-15.1 on model training.

sec-13.1 is the problem: Customer-only licence, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion, excluding Affiliates and contractors — fails the fallback. sec-13.2/13.3 (perpetual paid-up licence, limited revocation) are the internal counterweight to cite.
Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, Vendor bears cost absent >5% underpayment — consistent with our position; audit findings are our Confidential Information.

No liquidated damages or penalty payable by us is apparent; sec-7.3 limits interest on disputed sums. Any economic exposure sits in the sec-2.1 take-or-pay, handled under MINCOMMIT — do not double-flag.

sec-19.1/19.3 give solid services and compliance warranties, but sec-19.2 limits the Deliverable warranty to 15 days and cuts off all correction or refund duty afterwards — test that against the required duration; sec-19.4 supplies the remedy and sec-6 the acceptance backstop.
Clause present with CGL, workers' comp, employer's liability, E&O and USD 5,000,000 cyber cover, certificates on request, and no limitation of liability — check limits against playbook thresholds.

sec-2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000/year three-year take-or-pay expressly 'without reduction or termination rights' — a material deviation that also conflicts with sec-9.4 and the sec-12.3 disclaimer of minimum-volume commitments.

sec-11.1 requires immediate cessation of assistance and deletion of Customer Data with no export or migration support — deviation; contrast sec-11.2/11.3 (return in machine-readable format, certified deletion) and sec-10.1/10.2, and note the internal inconsistency.
